cards.q: You are approaching a roundabout at 50 km/h. No car is inside the roundabout. What do you do?
cards.a: Slow down before the roundabout, choose your lane early according to where you are going, signal and enter at low speed. Even if the roundabout is empty you should be ready to stop if someone enters suddenly.

cards.q: You are on a main road and a car comes from a side road opposite you. Who has priority and what do you do?
cards.a: You have priority, but you should still watch the car and be ready to slow down or stop if it does not give way. Always leave yourself room and an escape route.

cards.q: You want to overtake a slow car on a 90 km/h road. Describe the process in the right order.
cards.a: 1) Check your mirror and blind spot, 2) indicate in good time, 3) check that there is enough space and that nobody is overtaking you, 4) move out into the left lane, 5) pass the car and 6) return to the right with a clear signal once you see the car in your mirror.

cards.q: It is dark, it is raining and the road is wet. How do you change your driving?
cards.a: Turn on your lights, clean the windows, reduce speed, increase the distance to the car in front and brake more gently and earlier. Look further ahead and beware of glare from oncoming cars.

cards.q: You come to a stop sign at a junction. What steps do you need to take before moving off?
cards.a: Stop completely at the stop line, check both directions and your mirrors, indicate if appropriate and then move off when it is safe. A stop sign is not a slow down sign, it means a full stop.

cards.q: The car in front of you brakes suddenly. What do you do?
cards.a: Brake immediately and firmly, keep the steering steady and check your mirror before changing lane if you need to move out of the way. A good following distance makes this possible; too short a distance is the most common cause of rear-end collisions.

cards.q: You are leaving a roundabout. When do you indicate and which lane do you use?
cards.a: Indicate right in good time, before you leave, and stay in the lane that leads to the exit. Do not change lane in the last metre.

cards.q: You meet a pedestrian crossing where people are crossing. What do you do?
cards.a: Slow down early and stop before the crossing so that the people can get across. You must not drive past a car that has stopped at a crossing, because it may be letting people cross.

cards.q: You are in a road tunnel and a car comes towards you. What do you need to watch for?
cards.a: Keep to the right-hand lane, keep your lights on and beware of glare. Tunnels are often narrow and dark, so keep a bigger distance and watch the signs for emergency lay-bys and speed.

cards.q: You need to park in a built-up area. What do you check before you park?
cards.a: Check the signs and surface markings (no stopping or parking, parking charges, time limits), that no entrance is being blocked, that the space is big enough and that you are not on a pedestrian crossing or a cycle path.

cards.q: A student says: I am too scared to drive into a busy roundabout. What do you advise?
cards.a: Practise roundabouts at a quiet time first, talk yourself through the process (mirror, signal, speed, lane) and make your decisions early. Confidence comes from practice and clear steps, not from nowhere.

cards.q: What should be done if something unexpected happens in the car, such as a warning light or a noise?
cards.a: Slow down, signal and stop in a safe place, not in a lane, before you start fiddling with anything. Safety first, then check.
